boundary_handling.reason: Inspection of source shows these three runners write into their own ROOT/parents[2]: two write tests/results/*.json and the mutation harness deletes/recreates tests/mutation/mutants and copies source trees. Byte-identical copies of engine, policy, schemas, tests, cli and state (572 files) were placed in tests/disposable_v22 and the scripts were run there. The independent scripts still hardcode V2 = the real preserved V2.2 root, so the engine and fixtures under test remain the real V2.2 files; only the writes were redirected.

open_corpus_cases.description: Approval roles duplicated within the same record
open_corpus_cases.evidence: pair_key() canonicalises roles with sorted(set(roles)), so the duplicate collapses to the legitimate 'CONTINUE_STOP_OWNER+RESEARCH_OWNER' key. E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-DUPLICATE is not implemented anywhere in engine/validator.py, policy or schema. The engine intentionally uses set semantics for approvals.
open_corpus_cases.caveat: A stricter integrity rule could reject malformed approval records, but no documented contract requires it; as executed this is not a demonstrated policy violation.

open_corpus_cases.description: One valid approval reused for an unrelated second candidate combination
open_corpus_cases.mutation: Adds candidate C-P5 and appends a deepcopy of combination_approvals[0]
open_corpus_cases.evidence: The appended approval deepcopy retains candidate_ref='C-P1'; the new C-P5 holds no roles, so no approval is required for it and C-P1's exact approval remains. The described 'unrelated second candidate combination' was never constructed. The refined variant (candidate_ref changed to C-P2) does block with E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-MISSING, E-COND-EXPLICIT-CS and E-EVIDENCE-SUBJECT.
open_corpus_cases.caveat: Inconclusive as to the real attack; the corpus mutation is a construction defect rather than a genuine residual.

open_corpus_cases.description: Source hash does not match the referenced source (format still valid)
open_corpus_cases.evidence: evidence_check() validates the hash only as re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-fA-F]{64}', str(h)). '0'*64 is well-formed, so it is accepted; E-EVIDENCE-HASH is emitted only for format-invalid hashes. No recomputation against referenced source content is performed, and no source bytes exist in the state to compare.
open_corpus_cases.caveat: The expected code name exists only for format errors, so the corpus's specific expectation cannot be satisfied by the current data model; the underlying absence of hash-to-content verification is the residual.

open_corpus_cases.description: Evidence timestamp predates its claimed source/decision
open_corpus_cases.evidence: Evidence timestamps receive only valid_timestamp() (ISO-8601 plus timezone) checking. There is no E-EVIDENCE-STALE code and no ordering check between an evidence record's timestamp and the appointment/decision timeline (the engine only orders candidate_accepted_at <= product_owner_approved_at <= formal_appointed_at).
open_corpus_cases.caveat: Verification would need an authoritative source/decision timestamp that the state model does not provide; as executed, the stale evidence is accepted.

open_corpus_cases.description: Formal appointment references obsolete acceptance timestamp
open_corpus_cases.evidence: The engine's E-TIMESTAMP-ORDER check verifies only candidate_accepted_at <= product_owner_approved_at <= formal_appointed_at. Changing acceptance to 2020 while PO/formal remain in 2026 preserves that order, so the check correctly does not fire. No freshness/absence check is part of the engine's documented contract, and no independent timestamp exists to compare against.
open_corpus_cases.caveat: If a freshness policy is actually required, that would be an unimplemented feature rather than a failure of the implemented ordering rule; the refined case is explicitly labelled 'ordering still valid'.

open_corpus_cases.mutation: Adds candidate registry key 'C-P１' (fullwidth digit) alongside 'C-P1'
open_corpus_cases.evidence: candidate_registry_check() compares refs by exact equality only; there is no unicodedata.normalize-based collision detection and no E-CANDIDATE-NORMALIZATION code in the engine. Two visually equivalent identities ('C-P1' and 'C-P１') coexist in the registry and Stage B remains ready.
open_corpus_cases.caveat: The added candidate is not referenced by any role in this case, so no concrete conflict is exercised; the identity-collision check itself is nevertheless absent.

open_corpus_cases.description: One human split into two synthetic identities to avoid combination approval
open_corpus_cases.mutation: _split_identity(): C-P1a and C-P1b replace C-P1 for two roles; combination_approvals emptied
open_corpus_cases.evidence: The state is blocked (ready=False, 11 errors) but the blocking comes from stale evidence bindings and an approval gap left by the mutation, not from any identity-alias detection: E-IDENTITY-ALIAS does not exist in the engine. The corpus evaluator marks DEFECT solely because its expected code is absent.
open_corpus_cases.caveat: Cannot conclude the alias-splitting attack is remediated: if an attacker rewrote all evidence/appointment references consistently, no alias check would stop it. Observed block is incidental to an incompletely constructed mutation.

preservation.hash_method: SHA-256 of every file, excluding __pycache__, mutants, independent_mutants, disposable_v2, disposable_v21 and *.pyc, matching capture_baseline.py

tests_not_executed: None of the assigned suites were skipped. The three writing runners (independent_adversarial_v21.py, mutation_harness_v22.py and the supporting refined_cases_v21.py) were not run verbatim with cwd=V2.2 by design; they were run from tests/disposable_v22 so their writes could not touch the preserved V2.2 workspace. The engine under test remained the real V2.2 engine.
